thread:
elena: Quick heads-up — ran npm audit against main (console/ui). Found a high-severity issue in ssri (transitive, CVE-2024-XXXX) and a medium in tough-cookie via an old request-like dep. Lockfile change will be noisy if we do broad upgrades. Who can triage impact?
mike: I'll take a look. Is this hitting prod bundles or just dev deps? :thinking_face:
elena: Appears the vulnerable path is in the webpack pipeline — ssri is used by an older tarball extractor used during build (not runtime), so exploitability in prod is low. Still want to patch for supply-chain hygiene and CI noise.
parul: If it's build-only, our immediate risk is CI/attacker modifying build artifacts. We should prefer fix that doesn't change generated bundles. Can we apply a resolutions/overrides instead of full bump?
mike: For pnpm we can set overrides in package.json. For npm/yarn we use "resolutions" + npm-force-resolutions or patch-package. Example I ran locally:
```
// package.json
"pnpm": {
  "overrides": {
    "ssri": "8.0.1"
  }
}
```
then `pnpm install` and commit pnpm-lock.yaml. That kept bundle output identical.
jen: Note: patch-package is okay short-term but we should upstream to the bundler dep. Also need to update our upgrade checklist so we don't regress the override.
deploy-bot: CI job build:webpack failed — pnpm-lock.yaml mismatch between local and CI cache. :warning:
sam: That's the churn problem. If we change lockfile, a bunch of PRs will rebase and trigger pipeline runs. We should coordinate a quiet window or a batching PR that updates deps and updates snapshots.
elena: Proposal: 1) Create single "ui-bundler-cves" PR that applies pnpm override for ssri and bumps the minimal set to resolve tough-cookie. 2) Add a CI check that verifies deterministic bundle hash (hashes stored in artifacts/) to ensure no runtime change. 3) Backport to latest support branch if tests pass.
parul: +1. Also add an entry to our SBOM and audit log: indicate CVE, path, mitigation (override), and who approved. We should record KMS-encrypted approval for the backport — security policy requires signed approval for high CVEs.
mike: I have a local repro. Patch plan:
- add pnpm override ssri@8.0.1
- bump tough-cookie via tough-cookie@3.0.6 (transitive)
- run `pnpm install && pnpm -w rebuild` and run `yarn build:ci` to confirm hashes
If all green I'll open the PR and ping @elena for approval.
elena: Assign ownership to mike. Timeline: aim to get PR out today, review + merge tomorrow morning, and schedule a single coordinated deploy to avoid lockfile churn across many PRs. Label as security/urgent.
jen: I'll add a QUICK note in the release channel and block any non-security merges into main until the PR lands to reduce churn.
deploy-bot: Lockfile-checker job queued — will fail CI on mismatched pnpm-lock.json and report diff.
sam: One more ask — add a tiny test that validates node_modules tree for the fixed ssri version so we can't accidentally regress by accidental dependency resolution.
elena: Good point. Add an integration check: `node -e "console.log(require('ssri').version)"` in CI stage after install, assert startsWith('8.0'). That will fail fast.
mike: Will include that. Also adding a CHANGELOG entry under security with the CVE ids and mitigation steps.
parul: After merge, I'll handle SBOM update and mark the incident as mitigated in the audit log. We should also run a quick synthetic build in our dedicated infra to validate production bundles.
elena: Thanks — summary action items: mike open PR with pnpm override + minimal bumps + bundle-hash/test + ssri version check; jen freeze non-security merges; parul update SBOM/audit log and handle backport; sam add node_module version assertion; elena to approve and coordinate deploy. We'll reconvene in #eng-sre if CI shows any surprises. :thumbsup:
